author: NT3595
title: Could use some custom feature options
content:
I like this game but if you play it awhile you realize it could be improved. To play on your phone many puzzles do not fit entirely on your screen which means you have to move it around which in turn obscures other areas. The bigger the puzzle the more challenging. I like those but you can’t always pinch it small enough to see it in its entirety. I wish you could make it small enough to see all of it but keep the challenges of the bigger puzzles. Also, that often make it easier to make mistakes that you would normally see could you view the entire puzzle at once. 
I have small hands (fingers) and sometimes hit the wrong arrow line unintentionally. Because I sometimes have to have the puzzle as small as possible to see it all it is really difficult to hit the right arrow even with small hands. I would appreciate more size control to enlarge and reduce.
Finally, unless I’m doing something wrong I wish you could label a level and get consistent puzzles within that challenge option. The way mine works I can get several in a row that are small and hardly a challenge. That is barely worth the effort of putting up with ads because of how fast you’re on to the next puzzle. Only a few come in that are considered hard or more challenging. I would like a way to select that range continually.
I do enjoy this but would like it way better if these issues could be addressed.

author: Rodsaturkey
title: Arrows - Puzzle Escape
content: I’m not a frequent gamer with the exception of my language learning app, but I decided to download and try this arrows game for points on a rewards app. I actually really like it. When you first download it, games start simple and become progressively more complex; but after you hit a certain level of complexity, what level you will get next becomes randomized. You get three chances (hearts) to make mistakes before the game stops you, but all you have to do to resume play is watch an ad. Every puzzle has a solution - you just have to be patient with yourself and find it. And even if you get stuck and can’t see it, there’s a hint button. The dotted grid behind the arrows helps you visualize the rows and columns of play. There’s no timer, so you can play at your own pace, even stopping for hours and then picking up where you left off. Since I’m always on a timer on my language app, it’s super nice to just play without a rushed feeling. You can sincerely lose track of time, though. There’s no clock in any of the screen corners, and you keep telling yourself you’ll stop “after the next one,” which I’m sure is designed that way absolutely on purpose. That’s my biggest beef with this game, but I’m a big girl who knows how to watch another clock or set a timer, so this game still gets 5 stars from me.

author: RalphTomaccio
title: A good game for a short period of time!
content:
I’m into the second day of playing this game and am up to level 176 already, in addition to completing the daily challenges that I missed for the month. Being a detail type A person, I am finding this game rather easy. Although, I do make stupid mistakes occasionally by sometimes going too fast in selecting the desired arrow and missing it, hitting a wrong arrow instead which makes you lose a heart! Three hearts and you have to restart. I am beginning to get tired of this game mainly because there are only about a dozen or so different games and unlimited levels, which means you are playing the same set of games over and over again. BORING! Even the so-called extremely difficult levels aren’t really any more difficult, other than having more arrows crammed onto the screen. Some of the games are so easy that they can be completed in less than 30 seconds. Gets old quickly!

Suggestion: I would love to see a timer added to each different game that would start the moment you touch the first arrow and stop with the last. I would also like to have this timer persistent, meaning that it will appear with the time it took the last time you played that particular game so that you can try to beat your last time as well as the time for the current game. Your best time will always appear until beaten. This would make it a bit more interesting and another reason to continue to play this game.

author: Decorating Dreamer
title: Relaxing brain game
content: I play the Arrows game before I go to bed. It helps get my mind off of the day. I like how the levels go back and forth from difficult to easier. That is a nice quality in this game as it keeps it relaxing and fun. It’s feels like a good brain exercise, yet it keeps it fun and not overly difficult. After you finish a difficult one, it’s like a reward to then get an easy one. I don’t want the game to get increasingly more difficult, when I’m trying to relax. The simple black and white color theme is a relaxing feature as well. The game now rotates on my iPad, but before when it didn’t, I just played it with the screen sideways, it really doesn’t matter what angle it’s played from. Another review stated to always look ahead of the arrow to double check that the area is clear. That’s a good tip, especially with the more difficult ones where the arrow puzzle with continue past the screen. I’ve gone through a lot of different brain-game puzzles and I am now just playing this one!   I play the free version, There is an ad after a game, but I’m okay with that to keep it free. Hey, that’s how I found this game anyway, from an ad of a different game that I was playing.

author: Mmhalla27

author: Eilla_Doodles
title: Challenging yet fun.
content: It’s more or less that one advertisement you get about trying to make cars leave a parking lot, but minimalistic and a lot more in depth. There is a button to show the paths the arrows will take if you click on them, but this button does not show if they are invalid and is only really useful if you are trying to double check something due to the amount of lines that appear- which I think is actually a good thing, as it keeps the game difficult. 20 levels in you unlock daily levels, which you can play even if you have missed days or didn’t even have the app yet, which means plenty of puzzles you can do even though I would not be surprised if later levels repeat themself once you get far enough (which seems to be the norm with mobile puzzle games). While there is ads between levels, this is easily avoided with airplane mode. Nothing special, but if you have ever wanted to play a good take on that car ad, here is your game. I have heard the game can be buggy, but I have never seen that myself.

author: blue☁️cloud
title: The perfect game
content:

author: Meech324
title: OMG download now!!!!
content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Arrows - Puzzle Escape is one of the best puzzle games I have played in a long time. From the moment I started playing, I was hooked by the creative level designs and fun challenges. Each puzzle makes you stop and think, but the solutions are very satisfying when you figure them out. The game does a great job of introducing new ideas and mechanics, so it never feels repetitive or boring.

One thing I really like is that the difficulty increases at a good pace. The early levels help you learn how the game works, and later levels become more challenging without feeling unfair. It feels rewarding to complete a difficult level, and it keeps me wanting to play just one more puzzle.

The controls are simple and easy to understand, which makes the game accessible for players of all ages. The graphics are clean and polished, and the overall design is pleasant to look at. I also appreciate how smoothly the game runs and that I can focus on solving puzzles without distractions.

What makes Arrows - Puzzle Escape stand out is how it combines fun, strategy, and problem-solving. It is a great game for passing the time, exercising your brain, and challenging yourself. Whether you are a casual player or someone who loves puzzle games, there is something here to enjoy.

Overall, I highly recommend Arrows - Puzzle Escape. It is entertaining, well-designed, and full of clever puzzles that keep you engaged. I have had a great experience playing it and look forward to seeing more levels and updates in the future. Great work by the developers!

author: DyreLogan

content:

author: Wonderfulhuman
title: just the right level of challenging!
content:
the perfect game if you like low stress, satisfying gameplay with a side of challenge! i’m someone that doesn’t enjoy stressful gameplay, so i appreciate that the levels aren’t timed and vary in difficulty levels, instead of just increasing in difficulty. it’s nice to play a few easy levels after a more difficult one! even the most difficult levels are just challenging enough to be super satisfying when you beat them. i’ve never felt like a level was designed to be truly impossible, and it’s so fun figuring out that one arrow that makes the whole rest of the puzzle work after a minute of being stumped! as for the ads: i’ve noticed that they tend to play after every other game and after every nightmare level. that was fine by me for a while, but got a bit irritating after playing multiple games in a row. after playing this game for 3 weeks, i purchased the $10 ad free upgrade. i don’t mind paying a one time fee for a game without ads, especially since that’s a similar price to what id expect to pay for a game like this on a platform like steam. i’m glad it’s a one time fee and not a subscription like ive seen some ad free fees being!!! 

overall, a fun game perfect for someone with a low tolerance for frustration and a love of satisfying gameplay that isn’t just a farming sim or idle game!

author: Caramel slinger

content:

author: Ally_Ally_Bo_Bally
title: Great game!
content: The levels are engaging, the mechanics are smooth, and I love that there’s a dark mode. It ticks all the boxes for a game like this. My ONLY complaint is the hint button. Either hide it somewhere so I can go get it WHEN I need it (I don’t need it), or have it “always on” somewhere semi-discreet. If I take longer than ~10 seconds to pick out my next move, that button flashes on and it’s distracting (to me) and irritating. It suggests that I need a hint after 10 seconds, which is pretty insulting, since it’s a game of logic, so I NEED A SECOND TO LOOK AT THE OPTIONS. There’s this urgency in it, where I feel like I’m expected to be “smarter” and I’m suddenly racing to keep that thing from turning on at all and then I make mistakes. It’s a weird little psychological nightmare for me, honestly, but this is purported to be a “relaxing” game. That button is the opposite of relaxing for some nuero-spicy folk like me.

author: LilithWølf07

content:

author: Lisaine
title: Love this game
content:

That can’t be interrupted and it happens every time you touch the screen, even if you are 100% accurate with tapping the impossibly tiny target to close the ad.

author: Thusarik
title: Love this game
content:
I love this game, I get back to it several times a day. But there are several things I wish they would change. 

1: When you select the grid option, they don’t always put a grid line on every arrowhead. I wish they would put grid lines on *every* arrow head. That’s the whole point of asking for the grid lines.

2: Let us “pinch” in, so phone users can see the *whole* puzzle. If the whole puzzle doesn’t fit on the screen, it would be appreciated, if I could pinch it in so I could see the whole puzzle. So I could see where all the arrow heads are going. I’m not asking to make puzzles smaller, and easier. Do make them bigger and harder. I do want a more challenging puzzle. Just let us pinch it in, so we can see the whole thing and see where *all* the arrows are going.

3: Also, don’t make the screen so sensitive. Because none of my other apps are that sensitive. When I touch the screen to move it around, you take that touch as an error, as making a mistake. Racking up the mistakes and then making me watch an ad to get back in. Naughty. Stop it.

4: I would like to buy this, but 9.99 is just too much. 4.99 is as much as I will pay for an app.

title: Recent update
content:

title: Not fair for typo taps
content:
First, on a small phone screen there should be an undo opportunity for fat fingering or touch screen mistakes. Clearly I’m not going to purposefully tap an arrow that is completely landlocked. But when I tap and drag the screen to pan over, and it instead registers as a tap, that should not count against me.  If I had tapped an arrow without checking if the path was clear then I agree that should lose a heart. But today I lost a 1450 perfect streak due to trying to pan from left to right and it registering a tap that I never intended. 

Second, the red outline after you have made a mistake is not colorblind friendly. It makes it impossible to see other lines whether they are actually long arrow tails or crosshairs lines. 

This was my favorite game up to this point but now I’m so frustrated losing the streak unfairly that I may give it up.

author: DontSuckMyToes
title: This game is a metaphor for life
content:
I’ve never written a review on an app (I totally have but I just want to fit in with the other reviews). However, this game has made my mind draw a parallel between the game and the dilemmas of life. Every level has encoded the same feelings in pretty much the same order:
-I begin the level and I find all the easy arrows. I swiftly press each one, and I think I’m doing a good job and won’t have any issues.
-for a moment, I don’t see any arrows I can press. I feel anxious and stuck, looking all over the screen for an arrow, but to no avail. I feel like I’ve lost and that I must give up. 
-I finally find the arrow. The flow begins again. And I think to myself “why was I so anxious about that?”

It reminds me of my own experiences with life. It hits a little bit harder tonight because I had a pretty bad panic attack earlier tonight. It’s just like the cycle of anxiety we all experience. Things are going well, we hit a rough spot that seems difficult to get through, we feel like it will never end and we can do nothing, but we disprove ourselves every time. Perseverance no matter what. No matter how hard it gets.

There is a wide variety of levels and no level is impossible to do without power ups. There is a daily challenge level. The league system is really ingenious.
